from astropy.io.ascii import core
import contextlib

class RST2(RST):
    def __init__(self, header_rows=None):
        super().__init__(delimiter_pad=None, bookend=False, header_rows=header_rows)
    def write(self, lines):
        lines = super().write(lines)
        idx = len(self.data.header_rows)
        lines = [lines[idx]] + lines + [lines[idx]]

text = '''\
===== ========
 wave response
   nm       ct
===== ========
350.0      0.7
950.0      1.2
===== ========
'''
orig_init = RST.__init__
def new_init(self, header_rows=None):
    orig_init(self)
    if header_rows is None:
        header_rows = ['name']
    self.header.header_rows = header_rows
    self.data.header_rows = header_rows
    self.data.start_line = len(header_rows) + 2
RST.__init__ = new_init

t = ascii.read(text, format='rst', header_rows=['name','unit'])
print(t)
print(t.as_array())
print(type(t['wave'][0]), t['wave'][0], t['wave'].unit, t['response'].unit)
PY

args.summary:
Updated `astropy/io/ascii/rst.py` so the reStructuredText writer/reader supports the `header_rows` keyword.

Changes:
- `RST.__init__` now accepts `header_rows=None` and forwards it to the `FixedWidth` superclass, which stores it on both the header and data objects.
- `RST.__init__` also sets `self.data.start_line = self.header.start_line + len(self.header.header_rows) + 1`, so RST reading correctly skips the top border, all header rows, and the separator line for any number of header rows.
- `RST.write` now uses `n_header_rows = len(self.header.header_rows)` to identify the separator/border line instead of hardcoding `lines[1]`, so multi-row headers are wrapped with the correct top and bottom borders.

This makes `tbl.write(..., format="ascii.rst", header_rows=["name", "unit"])` produce valid RST output, keeps default single-header output unchanged, and enables correct read/write roundtrips with multiple header rows.
